extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate and graduate students in functional analysis / PDEs (Sobolev spaces and elliptic BVPs)
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook exercise list on Sobolev spaces and variational formulation of boundary value problems (1D and N-D). Contains concrete proof/computation tasks: operator properties, existence/uniqueness of weak/classical solutions, spectral analysis, eigenvalue asymptotics, density/extension theorems, and functional inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 5 (existence for λ ≠ λ0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that if λ ≠ λ0, then for every f ∈ L2(I) there exists a unique solution u ∈ H2(I) ∩ H1_0(I) of (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Consider the linear operator S : g → v where v is the unique solution of −v'' + v = g, v(−1)=v(1)=0; write (1) in the form u − λ u(0) φ = S f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 6 (analysis at λ = λ0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze completely problem (1) when λ = λ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Find a simple necessary and sufficient condition on S f such that problem (1) admits a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.1 Check boundedness of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the operator T: H→H defined by (Tf)(x)= x ∫_x^1 (1/t) f(t) dt + x ∫_0^x t f(t) dt (0≤x≤1) is a bounded operator on H = L2(0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.2 Prove compactness of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that T is a compact operator on H.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.3 Prove self-adjointness of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that T is self-adjoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.4 Positivity and injectivity of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that (Tf,f) ≥ 0 for all f ∈ H, and that (Tf,f) = 0 implies f = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.5 Regularity of u = Tf and compute u''
rubrics_metrics.description: Set u = Tf. Prove u ∈ H2(0,1) and compute u''; check that u(0)=u'(1)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check computed boundary conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.6 Determine spectrum and eigenvalues of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the spectrum and eigenvalues of T; examine carefully the case λ = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.7 Orthonormal basis (ek)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that ek(x) = √2 sin((2k+1)πx/2), k=0,1,2,... is an orthonormal basis of H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use question 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.8 Orthonormal basis (˜ek)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that ˜ek(x)=√2 cos((2k+1)πx/2), k=0,1,2,... is also an orthonormal basis of H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider ek(1−x).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.9 Compute Fourier coefficients αk(f) for simple functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f ∈ H and components αk(f) in basis (ek), compute αk(f) for (a) f1 = χ_[a,b], (b) f2(x)=x, (c) f3(x)=x^2 with 0≤a<b≤1.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.10 H1 characterization via components (necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume f ∈ H1(0,1). Prove there exists a constant a ∈ R such that (k αk(f) + a) ∈ ℓ2, i.e. ∑_{k=0}^∞ |k αk(f) + a|^2 < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use an integration by parts in the computation of αk(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.28.11 H1 characterization via components (sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversely, assume f ∈ L2(0,1) and that ∑_{k=0}^∞ |k αk(f) + a|^2 < ∞ for some a. Prove f ∈ H1(0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Set ˜f = f + a π /√2 and consider truncated expansions ˜fn; check L2 convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.1 Continuity and coercivity of bilinear form a
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that a(u,v)= ∫_0^1 (u' v' + u v) + (u(1)−u(0))(v(1)−v(0)) for u,v ∈ H1(0,1) is a continuous coercive bilinear form on H1(0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.2 Existence/uniqueness for associated variational problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that for every f ∈ L2(0,1) there exists a unique u ∈ H2(0,1) satisfying the variational equation a(u,v)=∫_0^1 f v for all v ∈ H1(0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.3 Show strong form and boundary conditions for u
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that u satisfies −u''+u = f on (0,1), u'(0)=u(0)−u(1), u'(1)=u(0)−u(1), and that any H2 solution of these strong conditions satisfies the variational equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.4 Operator T: self-adjointness and compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T:L2(0,1)→L2(0,1) be Tf=u (the solution). Check that T is self-adjoint and compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.5 Positivity preservation of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if f ≥ 0 a.e. on (0,1), then u = T f ≥ 0 on (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.6 Nonnegativity of quadratic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that (T f, f)_{L2} ≥ 0 for all f ∈ L2(0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.29.7 Determine eigenvalues of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the eigenvalues EV(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.1 Closedness of V
rubrics_metrics.description: For k ∈ R, k ≠ 1, set V={v∈H1(0,1); v(0)=k v(1)}. Check that V is a closed subspace of H1(0,1) and equip V with H1 scalar product.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.2 Continuity and coercivity of bilinear form a on V
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that a(u,v)=∫_0^1 (u' v' + u v) − (∫_0^1 u)(∫_0^1 v) is continuous and coercive on V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Show existence of C s.t. ||v||_{L∞} ≤ C ||v'||_{L2} for v∈V.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.3 Existence/uniqueness for variational problem on V
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that for every f∈L2(0,1) there exists a unique u∈V solving a(u,v)=∫_0^1 f v ∀v∈V.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.4 Regularity and strong form with coupling term
rubrics_metrics.description: Show solution u∈H2(0,1) and satisfies −u''+u − (∫_0^1 u) = f on (0,1) with u(0)=k u(1) and u'(1)=k u'(0).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.5 Converse: H2 solutions satisfy variational problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove any u∈H2(0,1) satisfying the strong form (2) is a solution of the variational formulation (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.6 Convergence of solutions with boundary parameter sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k_n→k ≠1, V_n={v∈H1; v(0)=k_n v(1)}. Given f∈L2, let u_n solve a(u_n,v)=∫ f v ∀v∈V_n. Prove u_n → u in H1(0,1) (and then in H2) where u is solution for k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: construct u^{(n)}(x)=u(x)+((k−k_n)/(k_n−1)) u(1) and compare; use bilinear form identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.7 Behavior when k_n→1
rubrics_metrics.description: What happens to sequence (u_n) if k_n converges to 1?

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.30.8 Operator T on L2: self-adjointness, compactness, spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider T:L2→L2 defined by Tf = u (solution). Show T is self-adjoint and compact; study EV(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.31.1 Eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of Sturm-Liouville operator with Neumann BC
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the eigenvalues of A = −u'' + u on (0,1) with Neumann boundary conditions u'(0)=u'(1)=0 and corresponding eigenfunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.31.2 L2 estimate for solution with zero mean forcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f∈L2 with ∫_0^1 f = 0, let u solve −u''+u=f with u'(0)=u'(1)=0. Prove ||u||_{L2} ≤ (1/(1+π^2)) ||f||_{L2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: apply question 6 in Problem 49.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.31.3 Contraction estimate for iterative scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Define sequence u_n by −u''_n + u_n = u_{n−1} with u_n(0)=u_n(1)=0, starting from u0 ∈ L2. Prove ||u_n − u0̄||_{L2} ≤ (1/(1+π^2))^n ||u0 − u0̄||_{L2} for all n, where u0̄ = ∫_0^1 u0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.1 H as Hilbert space with weighted scalar product
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V={v∈H1(0,1); v(1)=0}, H={f measurable and x f(x) ∈ L2}. Show H with (f,g)_H = ∫_0^1 f(x) g(x) x^2 dx is a Hilbert space.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.2 Existence of unique u_ε via weighted bilinear form
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f∈H and ε>0, check there exists a unique u_ε∈V satisfying ∫ (u_ε'(x) v'(x) (x^2+ε) + u_ε v x^2) dx = ∫ f v x^2 dx ∀v∈V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denote this u_ε.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.3 Regularity and DE for u_ε
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove u_ε ∈ H2(0,1) and satisfies −((x^2+ε) u_ε')' + x^2 u_ε = x^2 f with u_ε(1)=0 and a condition at 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.4 Integral estimate for u_ε'
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce |u_ε'(x)| ≤ (1/x) ∫_0^x t |f(t) − u_ε(t)| dt for all x ∈ [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.5 Boundedness as ε→0
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that x u_ε(x) and u_ε'(x) remain bounded in L2(0,1) as ε→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use question 1 in Exercise 8.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.6 Passage to the limit and existence of u in V
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass to the limit ε→0 to conclude there exists a unique u∈V satisfying ∫(u' v' + u v) x^2 dx = ∫ f v x^2 dx ∀v∈V.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.7 Operator T on H: self-adjointness and compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider T: H→H defined by Tf=u (solution). Check T is a self-adjoint compact operator on H.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.32.8 Determine eigenvalues of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine all eigenvalues of T. Hint: look for eigenfunctions of the form (1/x) sin(k x) with appropriate k.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.1 Existence of unique U in N with initial data
rubrics_metrics.description: For Sturm–Liouville A u = −(p u')' + q u on (0,1) with p∈C1, p≥α>0, q∈C, set N={u∈H2; a(u,v)=0 ∀v∈H1_0}. Prove there exists unique U∈N with U(0)=1 and U'(0)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: apply Cauchy-Lipschitz–Picard to Au=0 seen as first-order system.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.2 Dimension of N equals 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove dim N = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: construct V with V(0)=0, V'(0)=1 and express any u∈N as linear combination u(0)U + u'(0)V.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.3 Dimension of N0 equals 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N0={u∈N; u(0)=0}. Check dim N0 = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.4 Characterize N00 and eigenvalue 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Set N00={u∈N; u(0)=u(1)=0}. Prove dim N00 =1 ⇔ 0 is an eigenvalue of A with Dirichlet BC. Otherwise dim N00 =0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.5 Simplicity of Dirichlet eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that all eigenvalues of A with zero Dirichlet condition are simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: periodic BC can have multiplicity 2 (see Exercise 8.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.33.6 Extension when p∈C([0,1])
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend previous results to the case p∈C([0,1]) (not C1) by replacing N with N = {u∈H1; a(u,v)=0 ∀v∈H1_0}.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.34.1 Weak formulation for periodic boundary problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider −u''+u=f with u(0)=u(1) and u'(1)−u'(0)=k on (0,1). Find the weak formulation of problem (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.34.2 Existence/uniqueness of weak solution for any f and k
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that for every f∈L2(0,1) and k∈R there exists a unique weak solution u∈H1(0,1); identify the corresponding minimization problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.34.3 Regularity and classical solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the weak solution u belongs to H2(0,1) (and C2 if f∈C) and satisfies the strong problem (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.34.4 Maximum principle sign result
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that u ≤ 0 on (0,1) if f ≤ 0 on (0,1) and k ≤ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.34.5 Operator T for k=0: spectrum and multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Take k=0 and T:L2→L2 defined by Tf=u. Check T is self-adjoint compact and compute eigenvalues; prove multiplicity of each eigenvalue λ is 2 except the first one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: Dirichlet problem eigenvalues are simple, contrast with periodic BC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.35.1 Equivalence to fixed-point formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: For −u'' + a u' + b u = f, u(0)=u(1)=0 with given continuous a,b, set S g=v solving −v''=g with Dirichlet BC and show problem is equivalent to u = S(f − a u' − b u).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define S: L2→H2 by Sg = v.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.35.2 Compactness of operator T on H1
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider T: H1(0,1)→H1 defined by T u = −S(a u' + b u). Show T is compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.35.3 Fredholm alternative condition for solvability
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove problem (1) has a solution for every f∈L2 iff the only solution of homogeneous problem (f=0) is u=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.35.4 Uniqueness when b ≥ 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume b ≥ 0 on (0,1). Prove the only solution when f=0 is u=0, hence for every f problem admits unique u∈H2(0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: choose k>0 with k^2−k a − b > 0 and use a perturbation u_ε = u + ε e^{k x} and maximum principle argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.35.5 Dimension of homogeneous solution space and solvability condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that in general (without assumptions on a or b) the space of solutions of homogeneous problem has dimension 0 or 1. If dimension is 1, prove problem (1) has a solution iff ∫_0^1 f φ0 = 0 for some nontrivial φ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use Exercise 8.33 and Fredholm alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A1 Weak solution concept for 2x2 Dirichlet system
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2×2 system −u1'' + u2 = f1, −u2'' − u1 = f2 on I with Dirichlet BC u1(0)=u2(0)=u1(1)=u2(1)=0, define an appropriate weak solution concept and show existence and uniqueness u∈H1_0(I)×H1_0(I) for every f∈L2×L2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A2 Regularity up to H2 for components
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that u1, u2 ∈ H2(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A3 Classical solution for continuous data
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that if f∈C(I)×C(I) then u∈C2(I)×C2(I) and is a classical solution of the system with Dirichlet BC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A4 Compactness of operator T for the system
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider T: L2×L2 → L2×L2 defined by Tf = u. Check that T is compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A5 Eigenvalue set of T is empty
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that EV(T) = ∅ (no eigenvalues).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A6 Surjectivity and spectrum of T
rubrics_metrics.description: Is T surjective? Deduce that σ(T) = {0}.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.A7 Self-adjointness of T and computation of T*
rubrics_metrics.description: Is T self-adjoint? Compute T*.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.B1 Weak solution concept when prescribing Neumann conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the same 2×2 system but with Neumann BC u1'(0)=u1'(1)=u2'(0)=u2'(1)=0 (as specified), define an appropriate weak solution concept and check that Lax–Milgram does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.B2 Existence for ε-perturbed system
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ε>0, consider perturbed system adding ε u1, ε u2 terms and same Neumann BC. Show that for every f there exists a unique weak solution u_ε ∈ H1×H1 of (1_ε)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.B4 Boundedness in H2 as ε→0
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that u_ε remains bounded in H2(I)×H2(I) as ε→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.36.B5 Existence of H2 solution for the Neumann system
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that for every f there exists a unique solution u∈H2(I)×H2(I) of the original Neumann problem (1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.37.1 Identity operator as Hilbert–Schmidt
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the identity operator from H1(0,1) into L2(0,1) is a Hilbert–Schmidt operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: write u(x)=u(0)+∫_0^x u'(t) dt and apply previous problems (A3, A6, B4) and Problem 40.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.37.2 Summability of reciprocal squared eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (λ_n) be eigenvalues of −(p u')' + q u = λ u with Dirichlet BC; since λ_n→+∞, show ∑_{n=N}^∞ 1/λ_n^2 < ∞ for some N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: sharper estimates later (Exercise 8.42). Use asymptotics and properties from Theorem 8.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.1 Verify T maps into its dual and norm ≤1
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f∈L2(R) and unique weak solution u∈H1(R) of −u''+u=f (in weak sense), set T f = u. Check T(H) ⊂ T(H) (identify with dual) and ||T|| ≤ 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.2 Show EV(T)=∅ and check compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove EV(T) = ∅. Is T a compact operator?

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.3 Resolvent inclusion for λ∈(−∞,0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let λ∈(−∞,0); check λ ∈ ρ(T) (resolvent set).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.4 Resolvent inclusion for λ∈(1,∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let λ∈(1,∞); check λ ∈ ρ(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.5 Spectral inclusion σ(T) ⊂ [0,1]
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce σ(T) ⊂ [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.6 Non-surjectivity and 0 in spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Is T surjective? Deduce that 0 ∈ σ(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.7 Non-surjectivity of T−I and 1 in spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Is (T−I) surjective? Deduce 1 ∈ σ(T) and ||T|| = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.8 Surjectivity for λ∈(0,1) question
rubrics_metrics.description: Let λ∈(0,1). Is (T − λ I) surjective?

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.38.9 Conclude σ(T) = [0,1]
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude that the spectrum σ(T) equals the interval [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.1 Convexity and continuity of functional ϕ
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ϕ(v)=1/2 ∫ v'^2 + 1/4 ∫ v^4 − ∫ f v on H1(0,1), check ϕ is convex and continuous on H1(0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.3 Existence of minimizer u
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce there exists a unique u∈H1(0,1) minimizing ϕ.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.4 Euler–Lagrange equation (variational identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the minimizer u satisfies ∫(u' v' + u^3 v) = ∫ f v for all v ∈ H1(0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: compare ϕ(u) ≤ ϕ(u+ε v) and compute expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.5 Regularity and strong PDE
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove u ∈ H2(0,1) and u satisfies −u'' + u^3 = f with u'(0)=u'(1)=0 (a.e.); conversely any solution satisfies the variational identity. Deduce uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.6 Positivity preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if f ≥ 0 a.e. then u ≥ 0 on (0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use technique from Section 8.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.7 L∞ bound for cubic nonlinearity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that if f ∈ L∞ then ||u||_{L∞}^3 ≤ ||f||_{L∞}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: adapt proof of Theorem 8.19 using test function G(u − K^{1/3}) with K = ||f||_{L∞}.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.39.8 Variation with boundary-concentrated quartic term
rubrics_metrics.description: What happens when ϕ(v) is replaced by ψ(v)=1/2 ∫ v'^2 + 1/4 v^4(0) − ∫ f v ?

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.40.1 Infimum −∞ when mean of f exceeds threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Let j ∈ C1 convex with j'(t) ∈ (−1,1) and j'(t) ≥ |t| − C. Define ϕ(v)=1/2 ∫ v'^2 + ∫ j(v) − ∫ f v. Prove if |∫ f| > 1 then inf_{v∈H1} ϕ(v) = −∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take v = const.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.40.2 Boundedness of infimum when |∫ f| ≤ 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if |∫ f| ≤ 1 then inf_{v∈H1} ϕ(v) > −∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: decompose v = v̄ + (v − v̄) and use Poincaré–Wirtinger.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.40.3 Coercivity and existence when strict inequality holds
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if |∫ f| < 1 then ϕ(v)→+∞ as ||v||_{H1}→∞ so inf is achieved; every minimizer satisfies ∫(u' w' + j'(u) w) = ∫ f w ∀w and u∈H2 solves −u'' + j'(u) = f with Neumann BC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.40.4 Non-attainment when |∫ f| = 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose |∫ f| = 1. Show inf ϕ is not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: contradiction by integrating the PDE that would hold at a minimizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.40.5 Behavior of minimizing sequences when |∫ f| = 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what happens to a minimizing sequence (u_n) of ϕ when |∫ f| = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: show u_n = ū_n + (u_n − ū_n) with |ū_n|→∞ and boundedness properties of (u_n − ū_n).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.1 Existence of maximizer for quotient of L4 and H-norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Let q∈C([0,1]) and assume bilinear form a(u,v)=∫(u' v' + q u v) is coercive on H1_0 and defines norm |·|_H. Prove α = sup_{|u|_H=1} ∫ |u|^4 is achieved by some u_0 > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take maximizing sequence weakly convergent and use compactness to get strong L4 convergence; normalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.2 Positivity of maximizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Show one can assume u_0 ≥ 0 on [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: replace u_0 by |u_0| and use Exercise 8.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.3 Euler–Lagrange PDE for maximizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove u_0 ∈ H2(0,1) and satisfies −u'' + q u_0 = (1/α) u_0^3 with Dirichlet BC u_0(0)=u_0(1)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider variation w_ε = (u_0 + ε v)/||u_0 + ε v||_H and expand.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.4 Strict positivity of u_0 on (0,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce u_0(x) > 0 for all x ∈ (0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use the strong maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.5 Sign-definiteness of any maximizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u1 be any maximizer. Show either u1(x)>0 ∀x∈(0,1) or u1(x)<0 ∀x∈(0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: show |u1(x)|>0 on (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.6 Existence of positive C2 solution of nonlinear PDE
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce there exists u∈C2([0,1]) solving −u'' + q u = u^3, u>0 on (0,1), u(0)=u(1)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: scale u_0 by appropriate k>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.41.7 Nonexistence when form not coercive
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume a is not coercive: ∃ v1∈H1_0, v1≠0 with a(v1,v1) ≤ 0. Prove problem (3) has no solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: show λ1 ≤ 0 for first eigenvalue of A and multiply (3) by corresponding eigenfunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.42.1 Asymptotic estimate relative to constant potential
rubrics_metrics.description: For A v = −v'' + a(x) v on (0,L) with Dirichlet BC, let λ_n be eigenvalues. Prove |λ_n − (π^2 n^2 / L^2)| ≤ ||a||_{L∞(0,L)} for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: compare with operator A0 (a≡0) and use Courant–Fischer min–max principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.42.2 Change of variable to reduce general Sturm–Liouville to constant-coefficient form
rubrics_metrics.description: For general B u = −(p u')' + q u on (0,1) with p∈C2, p≥α>0, q∈C, introduce x=∫_0^t p(s)^{-1/2} ds mapping t→x and define v(x)=p^{1/4}(t) u(t). Prove u solves Bu=μ u iff v solves −v'' + a v = μ v on (0,L) for some a depending on p and q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: compute a(x)= q(t) + (1/16p)[4 p p'' − 3 (p')^2] after tedious computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8.42.3 Asymptotic bound for general Sturm–Liouville eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that eigenvalues μ_n of B satisfy |μ_n − (π^2 n^2 / L^2)| ≤ C for some constant C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of W^{1,p} ((Ω))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: W^{1,p}(Ω) = { u∈L^p(Ω); there exist g_i∈L^p(Ω) such that ∫_Ω u ∂ϕ/∂x_i = −∫_Ω g_i ϕ for all ϕ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω), i=1,...,N } ; set ∂u/∂x_i = g_i and ∇u = (g_1,...,g_N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: H^1(Ω)=W^{1,2}(Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9.1 (functional properties of W^{1,p})
rubrics_metrics.description: W^{1,p}(Ω) is Banach for 1≤p≤∞; reflexive for 1<p<∞; separable for 1≤p<∞; H^1 is a separable Hilbert space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: adapt Proposition 8.1 using operator u→[u,∇u].

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark on test function classes and mollifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Remark: In the definition of W^{1,p} we may use C_c^1 or C_c^∞ test functions; to show equivalence use mollifiers (ρ_n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Density/Friedrichs Theorem 9.2 (approximation by smooth compactly supported functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u∈W^{1,p}(Ω), 1≤p<∞. There exists sequence u_n∈C_c^∞(R^N) such that u_n|_Ω→u in L^p(Ω) and ∇u_n|_ω→∇u|_ω in L^p(ω)^N for all ω⊂⊂Ω. In case Ω=R^N the convergence is global.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses extension by zero and mollification; Lemma 9.1 about convolution with L^1 kernel commuting with derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 9.1 (convolution preserves W^{1,p})
rubrics_metrics.description: If ρ∈L^1(R^N) and v∈W^{1,p}(R^N) then ρ * v ∈ W^{1,p}(R^N) and ∂_i(ρ*v) = ρ*(∂_i v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt proof of Lemma 8.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 5 (Meyers–Serrin comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyers–Serrin theorem: for 1≤p<∞, u∈W^{1,p}(Ω) there exists sequence u_n∈C^∞(Ω)∩W^{1,p}(Ω) with u_n→u in W^{1,p}(Ω). For arbitrary Ω this may fail for global compactly supported approximations; compare with later Corollary 9.8 which assumes regularity of Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9.3 (characterization of W^{1,p})
rubrics_metrics.description: For u∈L^p(Ω), 1<p≤∞, the following are equivalent: (i) u∈W^{1,p}(Ω); (ii) ∃C s.t. |∫_Ω u ∂ϕ/∂x_i| ≤ C ||ϕ||_{L^p} ∀ϕ∈C_c^∞(Ω), i=1..N; (iii) ∃C s.t. for all ω⊂⊂Ω and |h|<dist(ω,∂Ω), ||τ_h u − u||_{L^p(ω)} ≤ C |h|. Moreover C can be taken = ||∇u||_{L^p(Ω)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses mollification/approximation and translation estimates; special case p=1 relates to BV functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark on continuity of W^{1,∞} representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If u∈W^{1,∞}(Ω) there is a continuous representative and |u(x)−u(y)| ≤ ||∇u||_{L∞} dist_Ω(x,y) for x,y in same connected component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9.4 (product rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u,v∈W^{1,p}(Ω)∩L∞(Ω), 1≤p≤∞, then uv∈W^{1,p}(Ω)∩L∞(Ω) and ∂_i(uv)=∂_i u · v + u · ∂_i v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by approximation with C_c^∞ sequences and dominated convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9.5 (chain rule / composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G∈C^1(R) with G(0)=0 and |G'(s)|≤M ∀s. If u∈W^{1,p}(Ω), then G∘u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) and ∂_i(G∘u) = (G'(u)) ∂_i u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by approximation u_n→u and dominated convergence; p=∞ treated by localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9.6 (change of variables formula in W^{1,p})
rubrics_metrics.description: If H: Ω̃→Ω is bijective C^1 with H^{-1}∈C^1, Jacobians and inverses essentially bounded, then for u∈W^{1,p}(Ω) we have u∘H∈W^{1,p}(Ω̃) and ∂_{y_j} u(H(y)) = ∑_i ∂_{x_i} u(H(y)) ∂H_i/∂y_j (y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by approximating u with C_c^∞ and composing; requires bounded Jacobian factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of higher Sobolev spaces W^{m,p}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define W^{m,p}(Ω) inductively: u∈W^{m,p} iff u∈W^{m−1,p} and ∂u/∂x_i ∈ W^{m−1,p} ∀i, equivalently all weak derivatives D^α u ∈ L^p for |α|≤m. Equip with norm ||u||_{W^{m,p}} = (∑_{|α|≤m} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p)^{1/p}. H^m=W^{m,2} is Hilbert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 8 (equivalence of Sobolev norms when domain smooth)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is smooth and bounded, the W^{m,p} norm is equivalent to ||u||_{L^p} + ∑_{|α|=m} ||D^α u||_{L^p}; moreover interpolation inequalities bound lower-order derivatives by higher-order ones plus Lp norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: R. Adams.
